title: Jeff Bezos: Amazon founder's consortium bought close to 40% of Liverpool
author: Aadam Patel
content:
![Jeff Bezos points to head](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1008/cpsprodpb/88c0/live/1f977b10-9b0c-11f1-bb80-c1b1e1adeea5.jpg)
Jeff Bezos is part of the 1892 Holdings consortium
- Published
A consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos bought close to 40% of Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group (FSG).
It was initially reported that 1892 Holdings had bought about a third of the club, but - as first reported by The Athletic, external - it is actually about 38%.
There is also an option for the consortium to buy a controlling stake in Liverpool in the next 12 months, though that does not involve a formal commitment.
In a statement on Friday, FSG confirmed it had entered into a "definitive agreement" for the sale of a "strategic minority investment" to 1892 Holdings.
The group - named after Liverpool's founding year - is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes Bezos and billionaire Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.
Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice-chairman and join an expanded board pending regulatory approval.
The son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal, he had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.
The deal is understood to value Liverpool between Â£5bn and Â£6bn.
summary: A consortium named 1892 Holdings, which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, has acquired close to 40% of Liverpool from Fenway Sports Group. The group is led by Amit Bhatia, who will become Liverpool's vice-chairman pending regulatory approval. The deal values the football club between £5bn and £6bn, and the consortium holds an option to purchase a controlling stake within the next 12 months.
key_points: A consortium including Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin bought approximately 38% of Liverpool.
Fenway Sports Group confirmed the definitive agreement for a strategic minority investment by 1892 Holdings.
Amit Bhatia leads the consortium and will join Liverpool's board as vice-chairman.
The consortium has an option to acquire a controlling stake in the club within the next 12 months.
The transaction values Liverpool between £5bn and £6bn.

title: Transfer news LIVE: Alvarez to Arsenal, Barcola bid, Fernandes talks
author: Alex Young
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![Bradley Barcola, Bruno Fernandes, Julian Alvarez]() The summer window is kicking into another gear as the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham work on deals to improve their squads before the start of the new Premier League season. The Gunners continue to be linked with Julian Alvarez and Victor Osimhen to bolster their attack, while Ezri Konsa and Jarrel Quansah continue to be of interest in defence. Man United are aware of interest in Bruno Guimaraes, amid reports of a £43million bid from Galatasaray, and are said to be interested in Adam Wharton and Kim Min-jae. Meanwhile, Liverpool have agreed personal terms with Ibrahim Mbaye as they take another huge step towards a double deal including Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola. Chelsea are braced for a Man City bid for Enzo Fernandez following Rodri’s move to Barcelona, while Pedro Neto has admirers in Saudi Arabia. Tottenham are closing in on the signing of Savinho and hope to then add Cody Gakpo to their forward line. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below! Latest transfer news and rumours Live updates Newcastle still keen on £50m Lucas Bergvall Newcastle United remain interested in signing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall. According to the Daily Mail, Matthias Jaissle’s side are considering Bergvall as a potential replacement for former captain Bruno Guimaraes. The 20-year-old is regarded as one of Europe’s most promising young midfielders, but earlier this summer asked to leave after not being guaranteed regular first-team football. Tottenham are understood to value Bergvall at around £50m. Liverpool to submit new Bradley Barcola bid Liverpool are set to submit a fresh bid for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola as they close in on a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye. According to RMC Sport, a deal to sign Mbaye is progressing quickly after the player reached an agreement with Liverpool over a five-year contract. Liverpool are also deep in talks over Barcola, with a new bid expected this week. PSG want a potential club-record fee for the France star. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/01KZRTW82CCT9NK9YH60MGADZ1.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Atletico send Alvarez transfer message to Arsenal after 'Arteta talks' Julian Alvarez has been left out of Atletico Madrid's first La Liga game of the season, but the striker remains not for sale amid interest from Barcelona and Arsenal. The Argentine has been Barcelona's top transfer target all summer, with the player having repeatedly voiced his desire to move to the Camp Nou. Arsenal have long been interested in the former Manchester City forward, with Mikel Arteta reportedly driving the club's interest, but it is Barca were Alvarez wishes to go. Atletico have other ideas, and have repeated privately and publicly ruled out a summer exit for the striker. “It’s like when you go to court, that’s it, there’s nothing more to it. We’re looking after both the person and the player, and we understand that he is not in the right condition to play in this match." ![Julian Alvarez](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/11/44/alvarez.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Tottenham set Richarlison transfer stance Tottenham will demand a sizeable fee if they are to sell Richarlison before the close of the summer transfer window, writes Sam Tabuteau. There had been concerns that Spurs could lose the Brazilian striker, who is attracting interest from Everton, on the cheap with a year remaining on his current contract. But Standard Sport understands that Spurs retain the option to extend Richarlison’s contract by an extra 12 months, meaning they will not be forced into a cut-price sale. Spurs signed Richarlison from Everton in a deal worth around £60million in 2022. Richarlison finished last season as Spurs’ top goalscorer in all competitions, netting 11 times in the Premier League as the north London club narrowly avoided relegation. Despite playing a pivotal role in Spurs keeping their Premier League status, the 29-year-old continues to be linked with a move away. A return to his homeland, or former club Everton, have been mooted. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/15/14/01M02V3KG7EVNXGMVVCAD3Z7V6.jpg?trim=0,0,226,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Man United, Newcastle and Tottenham monitor Edmond Tapsoba Manchester United, Newcastle United and Tottenham are monitoring Bayer Leverkusen defender Edmond Tapsoba. According to Fussballdaten, Leverkusen would be willing to discuss a deal for the 27-year-old centre-back at around €50m (£42.7m), despite his contract running until 2031. Tapsoba has been an important player for Leverkusen since joining from Vitória Guimarães in 2020 and has made more than 270 competitive appearances for the Bundesliga club. All three Premier League clubs are reportedly in contact with the Burkina Faso international’s representatives as they assess the possibility of a summer move. Chelsea demand £100m for Pedro Neto Chelsea are demanding a fee of £100m for Pedro Neto, Dom Smith reports. The Portuguese winger is attracting interest from Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, having also been linked with the likes of Manchester City, Tottenham and Liverpool this summer. However, Chelsea are not actively looking to sell Neto and would ask for an eye-watering £100m to entertain any prospect of a sale. Chelsea’s high valuation of Neto has been influenced by the inflated winger market elsewhere in Europe. Man Utd being new contract talks with Bruno Fernandes Manchester United have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insist he is not for sale at any price amid interest from Turkish giants Galatasaray, writes Sam Tabuteau. Standard Sport understands that United are determined to keep hold of their influential captain this summer and have held preliminary talks over a new deal. Fernandes’ current contract at Old Trafford expires next summer, but United, who have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, are relaxed about the situation and already in the process of negotiating fresh terms The Portuguese international enjoyed a stellar campaign last season as United qualified for the Champions League, breaking the single season assist record in the Premier League. Fernandes is viewed as a critical part of manager Michael Carrick’s plans. However, interest has begun to build in his services with clubs aware that he could leave on a free transfer next summer There was previously a £57million release clause in Fernandes’ contract, but that expired this summer and United have now made their stance on the former Sporting midfielder clear. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/17/20/01M087ESDKKD461P1X06HMC9VS.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Official! Newcastle sign Amar Dedic Newcastle have signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica in a deal worth around £30m. Dedic has signed a five-year deal to reunite with manager Matthias Jaissle, with whom he previously won the Austrian title at Red Bull Salzburg in 2023. "It's a special feeling and a really big honour for me to join Newcastle United," he said after the move was announced on Tuesday, his 24th birthday. "I'm really happy to be here and can't wait to start playing for the club and the amazing fans. "Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again. "Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started." Arsenal monitor Marc Pubill and attacking targets Arsenal remain keen to strengthen their defence and attack during the final days of the window. The Gunners made enquiries about Atletico Madrid defender Marc Pubill before the summer transfer window, but the Spanish club are equally determined to keep the 23-year-old. The Athletic report that left wing is Arsenal’s priority, though could move for a right-sided forward if the right opportunity becomes available. Kenan Yildiz and Julian Alvarez remain long-term targets, with Arsenal waiting to see if either becomes available before deciding whether to pursue alternative options. Manchester United open Bruno Fernandes contract talks Manchester United are in contract talks with Bruno Fernandes after the midfielder received a lucrative proposal from Galatasaray. According to The Athletic, the Turkish club offered the 31-year-old a salary of €20m (£17.1m) per year, but Fernandes wants to remain at United and is discussing a new deal. His current contract runs until 2027, with an option for a further year. A €65m release clause available to foreign clubs has also now expired. United are not open to selling Fernandes and maintain they have received no contact from other clubs over the Portugal international.
summary: Premier League clubs are actively working on summer transfer deals and squad improvements as the window progresses. Key developments include Liverpool nearing a double deal involving Ibrahim Mbaye and Bradley Barcola, Manchester United opening contract talks with Bruno Fernandes, and Newcastle United completing the signing of Amar Dedic from Benfica for £30 million. Meanwhile, clubs like Arsenal, Chelsea, and Tottenham face high valuations or resistance from parent clubs regarding targets such as Julian Alvarez and Pedro Neto.
key_points: Newcastle United signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica on a five-year deal for approximately £30 million.
Liverpool have agreed personal terms with Ibrahim Mbaye and are preparing a fresh bid for PSG winger Bradley Barcola.
Manchester United have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insist he is not for sale amid interest from Galatasaray.
Atletico Madrid have ruled out a summer exit for Julian Alvarez despite strong interest from Arsenal and Barcelona.
Chelsea have placed a £100 million valuation on Pedro Neto amid interest from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal.

title: Guardiola’s row with Walker at Manchester City revealed in new Amazon documentary
author: PA Media; Guardian staff reporter
content:
Pep Guardiola clashed with his captain and almost broke down in tears as he railed at players during his worst run as Manchester City manager.
Guardiola stood down at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. One of the lowest points of his glittering reign came during a testing run in the autumn of 2024, when City lost nine times and won only once in 13 games. Guardiola outwardly showed signs of strain, notably when he scratched his face after City surrendered a 3-0 lead to draw 3-3 with Feyenoord in the Champions League.
Behind closed doors he was also angry and upset with his players, as shown in a new fly-on-the-wall Amazon Prime documentary, A Beautiful Obsession.
At one point he argued in the dressing room with then captain Kyle Walker, who felt he was being unfairly singled out. “You keep saying my name in every meeting,” complained Walker after a defeat at Liverpool. “Every fucking meeting it’s my name. You’ve somehow brought my name into it.”
Walker, who had been voted captain by his teammates, also claimed Guardiola did not want him to be skipper.
Guardiola responded by saying Walker was taking the issue too personally but also showed signs of emotion as he explained why he had extended his contract despite their poor run.
“If I am a problem you have to tell me,” said Guardiola in a broken voice. “I won’t stay here for the money or just for the fact of staying. I extended my contract because I want to be with you. I want to fight. I don’t want you to feel like I’m leaving or running away.”
![Pep Guardiola speaking to Kyle Walker in a break in play when Manchester City played Spurs in November 2024. The two clashed when Walker was captain.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/661e1db928a879acc88f18e1cf001a908a4d6c8c/414_137_2666_1819/master/2666.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Another extraordinary outburst came in November 2025 after a dismal 2-0 loss to Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League. Guardiola, whose decision to make 10 changes had backfired, threatened to quit in the dressing room afterwards.
He said: “It’s unacceptable this lack of courage, passion and love and desire to win and do it better. I work for you. I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away, and everything for all of you. And what do you give back? The fucking performance you have done. It’s a disgrace guys. I’m really fucking tired. When I see that I’m exhausted, I’m drained. I want to quit.”
after newsletter promotion
Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the Manchester City chair, recently said Guardiola must have threatened to leave “100 times” during his tenure but he too had his concerns after the Leverkusen game.
In a remarkable release of voice notes between Khaldoon and the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, the chair said he was “so angry” after “probably one of the lowest points we’ve had”. Soriano said the response should not be “too negative or aggressive” but “not too kind or accommodating either”.
The four-part series, which covers the past two seasons, also includes some frank boardroom discussions about transfer policy and the long-serving Kevin De Bruyne’s disappointment after being told his contract would not be renewed.
summary: A new Amazon Prime documentary, "A Beautiful Obsession," reveals behind-the-scenes turmoil at Manchester City during Pep Guardiola's difficult managerial run. The footage captures a dressing room argument between Guardiola and then-captain Kyle Walker, as well as moments where an emotional Guardiola threatened to quit. The four-part series also documents boardroom discussions, transfer policies, and Kevin De Bruyne's disappointment over his non-renewed contract.
key_points: Pep Guardiola clashed in the dressing room with captain Kyle Walker after a defeat at Liverpool.
Walker complained that Guardiola unfairly singled him out in every team meeting.
Guardiola threatened to quit and expressed exhaustion following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Bayer Leverkusen in November 2025.
Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano exchanged voice notes expressing anger and concern after the Leverkusen match.
The documentary also covers Kevin De Bruyne's disappointment after learning his contract would not be renewed.
